title: Two men in court accused of stealing cufflinks from Prince William’s house
summary:
Albanians Mirgen Doku and Arilen Ndoci alleged to have broken into royal country mansion and also taken a clock

Two men have appeared in court accused of breaking into the Prince and…

blocks.text: Two men have appeared in court accused of breaking into the Prince and Princess of Wales’s country mansion and stealing six pairs of cufflinks and a clock.

Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, both Albanian nationals, were remanded in custody at Norwich magistrates court charged with burglary and trespass after a suspected break-in at the royal residence in Norfolk. A third suspect has still not been caught, the court heard.
Judge Bone was told immigration services were “not satisfied” with the status of the defendants, who are both homeless, and Doku had been sleeping in the woods near Anmer House.
The court heard they entered a dressing room at Anmer Hall by climbing a drainpipe. The items stolen were of an unknown value, the court was told.
One of the pairs of cufflinks alleged to have been stolen from the property was described as “the Duke of Edinburgh cufflinks”.
Damage could be seen on the exterior window frame, which prosecutors allege was from forced entry to the level where the dressing room could be located, the court heard.

The full allegations against the men were read to the court on Wednesday, including that motion sensors at the estate were triggered at 5.49pm on Monday. Motion sensors were also triggered near the window at the Orangery, and there were scuff marks on the drainpipe on the side of the building.
The court heard the men climbed the drainpipe to gain access to the dressing room. The charges were read to the pair as they stood in the dock and they were translated by the interpreter on the link.
Doku, of west London, and Ndoci, of no fixed address, were accused of entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site, police said.

The court heard the games and conservation manager at the Sandringham estate, David Harrison, was conducting a patrol using a thermal spotter when he saw two males jump through a hedgerow and run into a wooded area.
He followed in a utility motor vehicle but could not locate the men.
The court also heard the two men were later arrested without shoes on their feet and were taken into custody.
The judge, Matthew Bone, remanded Doku and Ndoci in custody and told them they would appear at Norwich magistrates court on Monday.

Queen Elizabeth II gave Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom country retreat, to William and Kate as a gift after their wedding. Police previously said specialist resources, including police dogs, drones and the national police air service helicopter, were deployed to assist with searches in the area after they received a call just before 6pm.
The secluded red-brick Georgian mansion is on the private Sandringham estate in Norfolk and is a short drive from Sandringham House, one of the king’s private residences.
It has a private swimming pool, a full-size, artificial grass tennis court and vast grounds.
Kensington Palace previously said it would not comment on security matters. It is understood no members of the royal family were at the property at the time of the alleged burglary.
